en.heading: 24–30 November: the history of Philippine National Book Week
en.origin: National Book Week in the Philippines invites readers to explore books, public libraries and the value of reading and publishing. The celebration lasts seven days and is distinct from a single international book day. President Manuel Quezon issued Proclamation No. 109 on 19 November 1936, establishing 24–30 November of every year as the national period for books and reading. The legal period falls in November, not April's National Literature Month. Those observances both promote reading, but they have separate historical and legislative origins.

en.purpose: Encourage reading, libraries, publishing and access to books across Philippine communities.

en.heading: July: Philippine Nutrition Month replaced an earlier March week
en.origin: Nutrition Month in the Philippines supports public understanding of adequate diets, healthy eating and malnutrition prevention; it takes place throughout July rather than on one health-awareness day. Presidential Decree No. 491 of 25 June 1974 created the National Nutrition Council; section 7 explicitly designated July Nutrition Month and tasked the council with approving and coordinating activities. The decree states that the new month replaced the previously declared Nutrition Week in March, making the earlier week a documented predecessor, not an extra current month-long observance.

en.heading: 25 November–12 December: why the Philippine campaign lasts 18 days
en.origin: The Philippine 18-Day Campaign to End Violence Against Women treats violence and exploitation as human-rights issues, encouraging prevention, victim protection and greater public understanding. Proclamation No. 1172, signed on 17 November 2006, established the annual period from 25 November to 12 December; it built on the earlier international 16-Day Campaign observed from 25 November to 10 December. The two extra days connect the campaign to 12 December, cited by the decree as the international anti-trafficking observance. The national 18-day period must not be collapsed into the original international 16-day schedule.
en.promoter: National Commission on the Role of Filipino Women and inter-agency councils against trafficking and violence are the institutions described in the historical state record as responsible for or associated with the observance.
en.purpose: Advance prevention of gender-based violence and informed support for survivors and their rights.

en.heading: 27 April: the National Artist distinction was created in 1972
en.origin: The National Artist establishment anniversary commemorates the creation of a state distinction for Filipinos who made exceptional contributions to arts and letters. It is the origin of an honor, not a personal artist birthday. Proclamation No. 1001, signed by President Ferdinand Marcos on 27 April 1972 upon the Cultural Center of the Philippines trustees' recommendation, created the category of Award and Decoration of National Artist. The proclamation also named painter Fernando Amorsolo the first National Artist. The award's founding history remains separate from commemorations of the births or deaths of later individual awardees.

it.origin: L'anniversario dell'Ordine degli artisti nazionali ricorda la creazione di un'onorificenza statale per contributi straordinari alle arti e alle lettere: non è il compleanno di un artista. La Proclamazione n. 1001, firmata da Ferdinand Marcos il 27 aprile 1972 su proposta del consiglio del Cultural Center of the Philippines, creò la categoria dell'onorificenza di artista nazionale. La stessa proclamazione nominò il pittore Fernando Amorsolo primo artista nazionale; la nascita dell'onorificenza è distinta dagli anniversari di nascita e morte dei premiati.

de.heading: 27. April: Der Titel National Artist wurde 1972 geschaffen
de.origin: Der Jahrestag der National-Artist-Auszeichnung erinnert an die Einführung einer staatlichen Ehrung für besondere Leistungen in Kunst und Literatur, nicht an einen Geburtstag.
